{{nymph|parent=[[Pacifica, Goddess of the Pacific Ocean]]}}Yangzi, God of the Yangtze River - Yangzi is a powerful and revered god, ruling over the Yangtze River, also known as the Chang Jiang, in China. He is often depicted as a majestic figure with a flowing beard, dressed in flowing robes, and holding a staff symbolizing his dominion over the river.

Yangzi is believed to be the guardian and provider of the Yangtze River, which is the longest river in China and one of the most important waterways in the world. He is associated with the river's life-giving waters, which sustain millions of people and countless species of plants and animals. Yangzi is also revered as a symbol of China's rich cultural heritage, as the Yangtze River has played a significant role in Chinese history, economy, and mythology.

As a god of the river, Yangzi is known to have both benevolent and wrathful aspects. He is revered as a protector of the river's ecosystems, safeguarding its diverse flora and fauna. He is also believed to have the power to control the river's waters, regulating its flow and preventing floods or droughts, which are significant natural disasters that can impact the livelihoods of those living along the river.

Yangzi is also associated with prosperity and abundance, as the Yangtze River is a vital source of water for agriculture, transportation, and trade in China. He is revered as a provider of fertile soil and favorable weather conditions for farming, and local communities often offer prayers and rituals to honor him and seek his blessings for bountiful harvests and economic prosperity.

Yangzi is also revered as a symbol of strength and resilience, as the Yangtze River has faced numerous challenges, including pollution, overfishing, and dam construction. He is seen as a guiding deity, inspiring efforts to protect and conserve the Yangtze River's natural resources for future generations, and promoting sustainable practices to ensure the river's health and vitality.
